name: Albanian

ancestors.notes: Isolated Indo-European branch; possibly descended from Illyrian or Thraco-Dacian

notes: Standard Albanian based on Tosk dialect. Unique Indo-European branch. Digraphs (dh, gj, ll, nj, rr, sh, th, xh, zh) listed before single letters. Ë = schwa /ə/. Q = palatal stop /c/. R = tap /ɾ/, rr = trill /r/.

sources.author: Coretta, Stefano; Riverin-Coutlée, Josiane; Kapia, Enkeleida; Nichols, Stephen
sources.title: Northern Tosk Albanian. Illustrations of the IPA
sources.publisher: Journal of the International Phonetic Association 53(3), 1122-1144 (open access; Edinburgh Research Explorer copy)
sources.notes: Consonant table with one orthographic word per phoneme (pp. 1124-1125) and the seven-vowel inventory (p. 1132), read in full; the variety is the Northern Tosk on which the standard is based. It corroborates ⟨th dh⟩ = θ ð, ⟨c x⟩ = ts dz, ⟨ç xh⟩ = tʃ dʒ, ⟨nj⟩ = ɲ, ⟨rr⟩ = r, ⟨ll⟩ = a velarised lateral and ⟨y⟩ = y. It disagrees with this map on four letters: ⟨q gj⟩ are laminal postalveolar affricates t̻ʃ̻ d̻ʒ̻ (qava, gjaku), not the palatal stops c ɟ; ⟨r⟩ is a retroflex flap ɽ (bari), not an alveolar tap; ⟨ë⟩ is /ɜ/ (për), which the authors use for typographic simplicity where the map writes ə; and ⟨o⟩ is /ɔ/ (por). Recorded here; the grapheme data is not changed in this citation.

location.notes: Glottolog's computed centroid for the Albanian family — a summary of a whole clade's range, not a place anyone speaks.
